metadata.case_name: CHAN KIN KA v. SIU TUNG HUNG AND OTHERS

injuries.description: Removal of traumatic cataract; intra-ocular lens implantation; corneal scarring and resultant permanent impairment of visual function of the left eye.
source: he underwent removal of his traumatic cataract on 28th July 1995 at Queen Elizabeth Hospital and stayed there for about a week.
An intra-ocular lens was implanted on his left eye on 16th August 1996 at the Hong Kong Eye Hospital.
A scar was seen at the time of Dr. Cheung's examination on 24th February 1999 measuring about 1mm x 2.5mm at the para-axial area of the cornea at around 1 to 2 o'clock position.
The left eye was pseudophakic i.e. the crystalline lens had been removed by surgery and replaced by an intra-ocular lens.
There was persistent blurring of vision in the left eye.

manifestations.description: There was persistent blurring of vision in the left eye.

The corrected visual acuity in the Plaintiff's left eye could be corrected to 6/9-; since the eye was pseudophakic, the visual acuity of the left eye was considered to be 44% i.e. half of 88% of normal and the permanent disability is thus 56%.
the Plaintiff was suffering from a 56% disability in the left eye which was equivalent to 30% loss of earning capacity and 28% loss of the whole person.
This meant that the patient could only see things far away but required reading glasses for close objects.

it would be dangerous for the Plaintiff to work at heights because of his impairment of judgment of distance due to the defective left eye; it was also dangerous for him to work outdoors in sunny conditions as the sun may cause glare causing transient blurring of vision; dangerous to work from heights or operating any potentially dangerous machinery.

treatments_received: Emergency repair of left eye (26th July 1995)

losses.description: the Plaintiff was suffering from a 56% disability in the left eye which was equivalent to 30% loss of earning capacity and 28% loss of the whole person.
I find that the Plaintiff could not have gone back to his pre-accident occupation as a construction worker doing painting work.
